proposed.explanation: Decreasing setpoints would further reduce artificial lighting, allowing work-plane illuminance to fall below 400 lux during monsoon months, violating code requirements and occupant comfort. Fixed setpoints ignore monsoon variation; artificial lighting would not activate sufficiently to maintain design illuminance, resulting in visual discomfort and potential code non-compliance during high-cloud periods. Disabling daylight harvesting abandons energy savings opportunities and creates unnecessary artificial lighting dependency; the system should adapt, not surrender, to seasonal variation. During monsoon season, when baseline daylight factor decreases 20–30%, setpoints should be increased to 450–500 lux to trigger artificial lighting earlier and compensate for reduced natural light availability. This maintains the 400-lux work-plane target despite atmospheric changes, optimizing the balance between daylighting capture and artificial supplementation. Seasonal setpoint adjustment (±15–20%) is critical for tropical daylight harvesting performance; understanding how monsoon cloud cover requires higher triggering thresholds ensures consistent occupant comfort across seasonal transitions.
